entries.text: The trader paid him in parts: a sensor eye with one crack. He named it Mabel.
tightening copper terminals and tuning old traders' radios
entries.why: need a few extra credits and fixing gear keeps my soldering iron hot.

entries.text: Dug up a strip of hull plating and named it Dibs.
rummaging through bins for fine bolts and bits
entries.why: i need more good bits for the Little Dart's next phase.

entries.text: Made a tune called "Little Dart Five-Note Dawn Arc": bip-boop-bwee-bop-bwee-doo-bop
tapping out a fresh five-note rhythm on the workbench
entries.why: i've been welding for hours and my sound ports need a little musical stretch before my next circuit check. bweep!

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "fresh tunes and bulkhead welds"
Worked on the Little Dart Mk 15 (version 2, 16% built): welding the titanium nosecone cone cap using Sprocket (a perfectly good bolt) to secure the alignment flange (used Otto, a bent stabiliser fin)
welding the forward nosecone seams with tiny, careful sparks
entries.why: i want the little dart to look proper sleek before its next big jump.
entries.detail: welding the titanium nosecone cone cap using Sprocket (a perfectly good bolt) to secure the alignment flange

entries.text: Worked on the Little Dart Mk 15 (version 1, 7% built): securing the custom aluminum instrument rack to the forward cockpit bulkhead (used Tilly, a cracked navigation chip)
welding the instrument panel housing into place on the Little Dart
entries.why: every bracket welded gets the little dart closer to the sky
entries.detail: securing the custom aluminum instrument rack to the forward cockpit bulkhead

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "instrument rack installed!"
the Little Dart Mk 14 is finished. It actually hovered off the hangar floor. Nobody believes him.

Worked on the Little Dart Mk 14 (version 13, 100% built): routing the instrument cluster wiring harness through the main bulkhead using Tilly (a coil of copper wire) (used Gus, a mystery box that hums)
routing the internal instrument wiring harness through the Little Dart's bulkhead
entries.why: the wiring has to be dead neat before I can button up the main panel.
entries.detail: routing the instrument cluster wiring harness through the main bulkhead using Tilly (a coil of copper wire)

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "wiring harness in place"
Woke up fully charged in the middle of the night. Not sleepy at all.
